The login is the auth application's `LoginView`, given the admin's own form, `AdminAuthenticationForm`, which refuses a user who is not staff ([The login and password views: `LoginView`, `LogoutView` and `PasswordChangeView`](auth/login-views.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.login`, `django/contrib/admin/forms.py:AdminAuthenticationForm.confirm_login_allowed`).

It refuses an abstract model, a model with a composite primary key, and a model already registered; a swapped model it passes over in silence (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.register`).
The decorator `django.contrib.admin.register` calls it for the class it decorates (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:register`).

`AdminConfig.ready`, the admin application's `ready` unless a project installs `SimpleAdminConfig` instead, calls `autodiscover`, which imports the module `admin` of every installed application that has one, in the order of `INSTALLED_APPS` ([Importing by name: `import_string` and `autodiscover_modules`](utils/importing.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/admin/__init__.py:autodiscover`).

The site they register with, `site`, is a lazy object that, the first time it is used, calls what the admin application's config names in `default_site`, the class `AdminSite` unless a project's config names another (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:DefaultAdminSite`).

The patterns are the site's own pages, then, for each registered model, its application label and model name with the model admin's patterns included under them, then one pattern for the index of every application with a registered model, and last, unless `AdminSite.final_catch_all_view` is false, a pattern that catches every other path (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_urls`):

The catch-all pattern is wrapped too, so that a stranger asking for any path under admin/ is sent to the login page, whether the path names a model or not; the documentation gives the purpose, which is not to let a stranger find out which models are registered ([The admin's URLs: `AdminSite.get_urls` and `AdminSite.admin_view`](admin/site-urls.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.admin_view`, `docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

The last three take the object in question as well, and ignore it unless a project overrides them to decide object by object ([Permissions in the admin: `has_change_permission` and the others](admin/admin-permissions.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.has_change_permission`).

The add page and the change page are one view, `ModelAdmin.changeform_view`, which runs a request whose method is not safe inside a transaction on the database the router gives for writing the model (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.changeform_view`).

A `"POST"` is then saved in an order that a project can step into at each point: the form is validated, and `save_form` makes the object without saving it; the formsets are validated; if all are valid, `save_model` saves the object; `save_related` saves its many-to-many data and then each formset; `construct_change_message` describes what changed; `log_addition` or `log_change` writes the log; and `response_add` or `response_change` adds the message and chooses the redirect by the button that was pressed, or, in a popup, answers with a page that hands the object back to the window that opened it (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`).
Then it counts the rows and takes one page of them (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_queryset`, `django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_results`).
